contract: spec/service/ACCEPTED_JOB.md (stage A1: the accepted-job contract, its Shen model and JavaScript implementation) and spec/service/HANDLER.md (stage A2: the handler in Fenrir, refining the A1 model; it runs on the draft TC1-D1 durable effects of spec/tc1/DURABLE.md and the Solo5 control protocol v2, spec/solo5/pure-call-control-v2.md). The contract is not part of slice TC1: the TC1 gate (spec/tc1/tc1-requirements.json) has no row for it.
aggregation: As the TC0-A and TC1 gates (TC0-GATE, 02 §14): any required row FAIL -> FAIL; else any BLOCKED -> BLOCKED; else any UNKNOWN -> UNKNOWN; else PASS. A mutant caught by no property, or a flagged equivalent control, is FAIL; a truncated exploration is never PASS. An evaluator error or a check that does not report is UNKNOWN. Every row's reasons are reported whatever the aggregate.
scope: Accepted-job bounded exploration at 2 tenants, 2 keys, 2 payload digests; per schedule at most 3 submits, 2 deliveries, 2 responses and 1 crash; state cap 2,000,000 (the default of harness/run-service-explore.sh and harness/run-service-fenrir.sh). The evaluator pins this scope, the A1 model's 251,374 product states, the 629,165 runtime edges the model and the JavaScript implementation must share, the mutants of each exploration, and the 22 and 13 retained counterexamples.

The Shen/JIT executable and library directory the gate runs on resolve to the flake's shen-jit output. No nix or no such flake output: BLOCKED. Another executable: UNKNOWN.

node --test tests/service/*.test.mjs: no failures (the JavaScript implementation against the hand-derived traces and small hand-derived exploration counts, and the manifest structure). Any skipped test is UNKNOWN.

harness/service-explore.shen at the scope above, JavaScript side sandboxed: the hand traces agree; the Shen model's exploration is complete and not truncated (251,374 product states) with no violation of any property; each of the 9 mutants is caught by at least one property and passes its prediction check; the equivalent control is caught by none; every property and every check fails on some mutant. A truncated or incomplete exploration, another scope, or another set of mutants is UNKNOWN; a violation, a mutant caught by nothing or a flagged control is FAIL; no report is UNKNOWN. model: models/service/accepted-job.shen and models/service/accepted-job-properties.shen (A1), models/service-a2/store-contract.shen (A2), run in-process by the Shen harness on the flake-pinned Shen/JIT with the TC1-D1 durable model models/tc1/durable-machine.shen
not_covered: The correspondence between the Shen model and the Rocq A0 model (by reading, not proved) and any proof of the properties: everything here is bounded exploration at the stated scope (2 tenants, 2 keys, 2 digests, small budgets), not a proof and not an unbounded refinement claim. The mutants and their predictions are written by the same author lineage as the model; the equivalent control shows only that the monitor does not flag one behaviour-preserving variant. The handler runs on the draft TC1-D1 durable effects (spec/tc1/DURABLE.md: owner choices unconfirmed, capabilities forgeable), so wrong-tenant is caught dynamically, not refused. The host is the A1 store under the stated storage contract (HANDLER.md section 3, owner choices in section 6 unconfirmed), not a real database (stage A3). The Solo5 row covers the distinct runs of the handler under quick mode (one replay per tape, no hostile-host or tape-negative tests); the full guest checks are the optional TC1 row durable-guest, which does not run the handler. Progress holds only under the stated delivery-fairness and availability assumptions. The contract is not part of slice TC1, and a pass of this gate says nothing about it. Stage A3 (host/service: SQLite under an OTP supervisor, the handler as a Solo5 worker) is covered only by the optional row a3-host-quick, in quick mode: observed history accepted over a bounded crash campaign, not a proof; power loss and fsync are not simulated, so the sync_off mutant is not detected; SQLite, OTP and the tender are trusted; one request per boot over a finite request domain; the host contract is a draft (ledger row SERVICE-A3-HOST).
